### 1. Scene
A small rectangular portion of cheese-topped lasagna or similar baked pasta, with a mixed-leaf side salad.

### 2. Vessel
A large, roughly square dinner plate, about **27 cm across**. Using the requested circular approximation gives an effective area of **3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm²**.

### 3–7. Items, area, volume, weight and energy
The salad includes green and purple leaves, a little shredded carrot, a few pale nut-like pieces, and a light dressing sheen. The pasta’s cheese and sauce are included in its estimate.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cheese-topped baked pasta | 14% | 80 cm² × 2 cm = 160 ml | 0.95 | 152 g | 180 | 274 kcal |
| Mixed salad leaves | 24% | 137 cm² × 2.5 cm = 343 ml | 0.15 | 51 g | 20 | 10 kcal |
| Shredded carrot | 1% | 5.7 cm² × 0.5 cm = 2.9 ml | 0.6 | 2 g | 41 | 1 kcal |
| Nut pieces | 1% | 5.7 cm² × 0.7 cm = 4 ml | 0.6 | 2 g | 650 | 13 kcal |
| Light oily dressing | Overlapping salad | Approximately 4 ml | 1.0 | 4 g | 450 | 18 kcal |

**Area check:** Food covers approximately **40%** of the plate; dressing overlaps the salad rather than adding coverage.

### 8. Sanity check
The estimate totals **about 211 g and 316 kcal**, plausible for a small baked-pasta portion and a loose side salad. Pasta thickness and dressing quantity are the main uncertainties.
